registered: 2026-11-17, before any run. Source: audit/sim_min.py (400 Monte Carlo draws of the unknown overheads) widened for model gaps, plus closed forms.
model: lambda <= (60/T) * min(M/r, S), T = 2.0 min. r = test jobs per landed change; S = independent lanes (cell 2: 1).

closed_form_hard_bounds_per_h.1a: 30 * 4 / 2 = 60 (r = 2: PR CI + one queue build per change)

assumptions: Job start latency U(10,30) s per job. It is hidden for jobs that are already started and waiting on a token (PR CI at t=0, agent jobs), and NOT hidden for each merge_group build, which GitHub only creates when a build slot frees.
Token / claim hand-off polling interval U(3,10) s per run; the waiter sees a release after U(0, interval). Release/claim ref push 1-3 s.
Test wrapper (cilock or harness) inside the token adds U(2,8) s per test job; the token-held minutes below include it (2.0 + wrapper).
Land Action: lock U(1,3) s + merge U(2,3) s, serialized; never the binding term (ceiling about 700/h).

Merge queue: PR CI pass to enqueue U(3,15) s; entry to merge_group workflow trigger U(5,25) s; build pass to group merge U(3,10) s, merged in order. Builds in flight = tokens given to the queue (a slot is held until merge). If the harness sets max_entries_to_build above the queue's token count the start latency partly hides and 1a rises toward its 60/h bound.
1b: groups of up to 5 are formed from entries waiting when a slot frees (GitHub grouping, one build per group). ALLGREEN (1a) is one entry per group.
Token split chosen by the 10-PR TUNING run among {1/3, 2/2, 3/1}; modelled as the best whole-run rate. Predicted choice: 1a -> 2/2 (about 100%), 1b -> 3/1 (about 90%), 2/2 (about 10%).
Cell 2 claim-only: claim CAS 1-3 s; with probability 0.5 the waiting agent's job start latency is not overlapped with the previous test.

Landed/h is (n-1)/span over the 10th to 90th percentile landings. With constant T and tokens released together, landings arrive in waves; that fence-post effect can push a token-bound cell slightly ABOVE 60*M/T, which is why 1c's interval extends past 120.
No GitHub rate-limit or abuse throttling, no failures, no cancelled runs, sufficient hosted-runner concurrency (at least 12 concurrent jobs) are assumed. Violations lower every number.

1b_queue_headgreen_group5_M4.note: bimodal: about 84-88/h if the tuning run picks 3/1, about 56/h if it picks 2/2

1c_agents_M4.note: median is above the 120/h token bound only because of the wave fence-post effect; the sustained rate is 100-115/h

2_claim_only_M8.note: same distribution as M=4: the cell tests that doubling machines does not move a serial lane

derived_claims_to_test.1c_over_1a: about 2.7x (interval 2.0-3.4x), versus the closed-form ratio of 2
